newsitem.title: JAPAN: UN's Akashi says N.Korea needs more food aid--KCNA.
newsitem.headline: UN's Akashi says N.Korea needs more food aid--KCNA.

text.p: A top United Nations official said North Korea needed more food aid after visiting a flood-hit area south of its capital of Pyongyang, North Korea's state-run media said on Thursday.
In a report seen in Tokyo, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said Under-Secretary General Yasushi Akashi toured the farming district of Unpha, south of Pyongyang, on Wednesday.
KCNA said Akashi, head of the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs and emergency relief coordinator, understood the extent of North Korea's flood damage.
"He felt an urgent need for the international community to redouble humanitarian support to people in the flood-hit areas who are scarcely living on a little food," KCNA said.
North Korea has asked for food aid from South Korea as well as from the United Nations following two years of heavy summer rains which washed away a substantial part of its rice paddy acreage.
Akashi, who has served as top U.N. mediator in the former Yugoslavia and Cambodia, arrived in North Korea on Tuesday for a four-day stay. He is to visit South Korea on Saturday and Japan next week.
